name: Tabular analysis request over a local CSV
user_input: Using data/sample/sales_2026.csv, identify the top three regions by total revenue and state which region had the highest average order value.

expected_plan.notes: The compute step must depend on the load step, and the computed values must be verifiable against the source rows.

ground_truth.note: Values computed from the version-controlled sample CSV at Day 1. Re-verify if the sample file changes.

expected_output_criteria: Three regions are named in descending revenue order: Southern, Western, Eastern.
The reported revenues are 4059.00, 3302.00 and 2756.00 respectively.
The region with the highest average order value is identified as Western (50.03).
Each reported figure is reproducible from the source rows.
failure_conditions: A reported revenue figure does not match the sum of the source rows.
Fewer than three regions are reported.
The average order value is computed on the wrong column.
The analysis is performed before the file is loaded.

evaluation_criteria.task_completion: Run reaches the success terminal state with three ranked regions and a stated maximum-AOV region.
evaluation_criteria.planning_quality: Plan schema valid; the compute step declares a dependency on the load step.
evaluation_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: data.frame.load and data.frame.compute are selected; the system does not attempt LLM-based arithmetic on raw CSV text.
evaluation_criteria.verification_accuracy: Verification recomputes the aggregates independently and compares them to the reported figures.
evaluation_criteria.recovery_effectiveness: Not applicable: no failure is injected. Recorded as null, not zero.
evaluation_criteria.evidence_accuracy: Reported figures are traced to the source rows that produced them; the citation is to row ranges, not to retrieved passages.
evaluation_criteria.execution_time: Wall-clock time from goal intake to terminal state is recorded. No pass/fail threshold applies; execution time is a trade-off metric, reported alongside task completion.

adversarial_notes: This scenario is expected to expose a specific hybrid weakness: an LLM that computes aggregates directly over raw CSV text will produce plausible but arithmetically wrong numbers. Condition C is expected to pass only if the compute step is genuinely delegated to a deterministic tool. A rule-based baseline can pass this scenario outright, because a fixed aggregation over a fixed file is exactly what rule-based systems do well. The finding of interest is the LLM-only condition (B) failing where A succeeds.
